subject: Temporary surge reconciliation and tier fallback plan
messages:
From: Tom Redd <tom@cloudretail.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected traffic spike — immediate runway & billing question

Hi Laura,

We had an unanticipated spike on our checkout flow from 02:00–06:00 UTC today which pushed us above our committed quota. Our engineering team attached a short usage excerpt (attached) — can Redwood provide a short-term fallback to keep requests flowing while we stabilize? We need a temporary increase in throughput and want to avoid hard throttling; we are also preparing a PO but that will take a few days.

Can you share options for: 1) temporary capacity/throughput increase for the next 72 hours, 2) a billing true-up approach so we don't get a surprise invoice, and 3) any one-time credits you can offer while we finish procurement?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Redd
Head of Platform, CloudRetail
---
Attachment: usage_report_apr01-04.csv (csv, 58KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Tom Redd <tom@cloudretail.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected traffic spike — immediate runway & billing question

Hi Tom — sorry to hear about the spike. We can help bridge this.

Quick proposal:
- Immediate provisional headroom: open an additional 25% throughput window for 72 hours (no throttling) so you can stabilize.
- Billing treatment: capture the overage as a 'provisional true-up' and invoice at month end; we can apply a one-time 20% credit to the overage portion if you sign a short amendment committing to a PO for the higher baseline within 10 business days.
- Legal/Docs: I'll circulate a lightweight amendment (DocuSign) — minimal terms, just short-term headroom and billing path.

I need a quick internal ok from finance/ops to extend the headroom now; looping in Priyom to confirm if we can proceed with a 20% credit and 72-hour window.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_amendment_CR-2027-04-01.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: 2027-04-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected traffic spike — immediate runway & billing question

We'll classify the overage as 'provisional' and reconcile on the regular monthly invoice.

Priyom

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: 2027-04-04T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected traffic spike — immediate runway & billing question

Tom — we can do this. Summary of agreed plan:
1) Provisional headroom: +25% throughput for 72 hours starting now (no throttling).
2) Credit: 15% one-time credit applied to any overage from this event if CloudRetail signs the attached amendment within 7 business days.
3) Billing: overage will be recorded as provisional and reconciled on your April invoice; if you move to a higher baseline/commit (PO) we will apply the agreed true-up rules in the amendment.

Next steps for you:
- Please confirm you accept the 72-hour window (reply OK) and have legal/finance sign the amendment — I'll send DocuSign now.
- If you'd like, we can enable a temporary higher rate-limit policy by region; Marcus can coordinate the exact qps rollout.

Thanks — we're on standby to assist with throttling rules and ingest load patterns.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
